full_judgment:
3. It appears from the decree of the Court of appeal below that the decree-holder opposite party obtained a decree declaring her title in the suit land and recovery of khas possession in 10 decimals out of the same by removing the defendant-petitioner therefrom. It further appears from the schedule of the writ of delivery of possession that the said 10 decimals of land has been mentioned as to be situated by the side of 29 decimals of acquired land from the southern side of the CS plot No.8. There should have been no difficulty to find out the side land on the part of the bailiff specially when there was structure of judgment-debtor-petitioner standing thereon. 

 5. As to the objection regarding non- specification of the said 10 decimals of land in the appellate decree it is necessary to mention that out of 96 decimals of land of the suit plot No.8 an area of 29 decimals from the southern side was acquired by the Government for road and plaintiffs title in the remaining 67 decimal has been decreed. As the judgment-debtor-petitioner forcibly dispossessed the decree-holder opposite party from 10 decimals of land from the southern side of suit land during pendency of the suit, she filed an application on 13.4.77 for recovery of khas possession in the said land. Court of appeal below after detailed consideration of the same, declared title of the opposite party in the entire 67 decimals of suit land and directed to deliver possession to her in the said 10 decimals of land by removing the petitioner therefrom there is no vagueness in the decree. If it is read with the appellate judgment and decree of the trial Court then it becomes clear to understand. Whenever executing court finds any difficulty to understand the decree it can look to the relevant judgment which gave rise to the decree for clarification and appreciating the decree properly. It is not for fun that a decree is passed by the Court. Court always passes a decree to give relief to the aggrieved party. So on technical and flimsy grounds execution of the decree should not be frustrated. Moreover petitioner's claim of title in the suit land having been negative by the Court of appeal below he cannot object to delivery of possession from 10 decimals of land from which he has been directed to be removed raising flimsy objection of non- specification of the said land in the appellate decree. I, therefore, find no merit in the contentions raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner and no illegality in the impugned order resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.
